key_insight: CAVQS reduces two-qubit gate counts by optimizing across circuit-block boundaries and exploiting permitted terminal measurements with classical feedforward.
engineering_relevance: Lower two-qubit gate counts could reduce execution cost and noise exposure, while dynamic implementations require measurement and feedforward support.
method: Redistribute unitary factors between overlapping blocks using QR decomposition while preserving the overall transformation.
Search for ancilla-free dynamic implementations before permitted terminal measurements under a CNOT budget.
Construct branch unitaries analytically to minimize expected CNOT cost.
evidence_signal: On common successful random-circuit instances, mean two-qubit gate reductions span 2.05%–74.64% across three baselines; on 4–6-qubit algorithm benchmarks, reported reductions span 20.65%–71.88%.
watch_item: Comparisons on common successful instances do not establish overall synthesis success rates, and dynamic-circuit latency may offset gate savings.
paper_title: CAVQS: Context-Aware Variational Quantum Circuit Synthesis via Unitary Redistribution and Dynamic Reconstruction
